items.title: 67559_Art Hodes oral history interview
items.q: Solo Art was -- at that time he had recorded four black pianists, Cripple Clarence Loften, Jimmy Yancy, Pete Johnson, Albert Ammons, I think, and maybe Meade Lux Lewis.

ctx.x: Jazz Information. There was another magazine called Jazz -- I can't think of it -- the Record Changer. That was in vogue. And they were more interested in discovering who was doing what on what record, and on what serial number and so forth on it, like a discography.

And Jazz Information also, but Jazz Information was also doing these articles, yes, and news. Then here comes Dan Qualey, with his Solo Art label. Solo Art was -- at that time he had recorded four black pianists, Cripple Clarence Loften, Jimmy Yancy, Pete Johnson, Albert Ammons, I think, and maybe Meade Lux Lewis. But they all had been on his label, and now he wanted to record George Zack, and this is the story of how I happened -- no, Dan decided to give me a date. No, that's -- I'm almost mixed up. He gave me a…

And I made 'South Side Shuffle' and 'Ross Tavern Boogie' because everybody -- by that time, the jazz people were hanging around Ross Tavern all the time. I can't think -- this fellow Brooks was singing every now and then and hanging around, and it was really a small group, and that was the big hangout. Every once in a while, Jimmy Ross would send a beer down, and it was a dismal basement. The water bugs were yay long, as big as your thumb, and there was a cat that would chase them around.
